:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: The curve $C$ is the intersection of a surface $S,$ defined by $z=f(x,y),$ with the plane $y=\pi.$ Given that the point $P(1,\pi,-1)$ lies on $C,$ and that $f_x = y\cos(xy) + \cos y,$ find the equations of the tangent line to $C$ at $P.$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z = f(x,y)$ with the plane $y=\pi.$ So, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $P(1,\pi,-1)$ will be given by the partial derivative $\dfrac {\partial z} {\partial x} \Bigg|_{(1,\pi)}.$ 

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative $\dfrac {\partial z} {\partial x}$ at $(1,\pi)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x}{|}_{(1,\pi )} & =\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(1\cdot \pi )+\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi  \\  & =\pi (-1)+(-1) \\  & =-\pi -1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-z{|}_{(1,\pi )} & =\frac{∂z}{∂x}{|}_{(1,\pi )}(x-1) \\ z-(-1) & =(-\pi -1)(x-1) \\ z+1 & =(-\pi -1)x+\pi +1 \\ z & =-(\pi +1)x+\pi \end{aligned}
$$

The equation above represents a line in the $xz$-plane. The $xz$-plane through the point $P(1,\pi,-1)$ has the equation $y=\pi.$

So, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(1,\pi,-1)$ is given by the intersection of the following planes:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y=\pi  \\ z=-(\pi +1)x+\pi \end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: The curve $C$ is the intersection of a surface $S,$ defined by $z=f(x,y),$ with the plane $x=1.$ Given that the point $P(1,2,4)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{y}=\frac{3x+y}{\sqrt{6xy+{y}^{2}}}$, find the equations of the tangent line to $C$ at $P.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z=f(x,y)$ with the plane $x=1.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $P(1,2,4)$ will be given by the partial derivative $\frac{∂z}{∂y}{|}_{(1,2)}.$

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative $\frac{∂z}{∂y}$ at $(1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(1,2) & =\frac{3(1)+(2)}{\sqrt{6(1)(2)+(2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{16}} \\  & =\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-z{|}_{(1,2)} & =\frac{∂z}{∂y}{|}_{(1,2)}(y-2) \\ z-4 & =\frac{5}{4}(y-2) \\ z & =\frac{5}{4}y+\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(1,2,4)$ can be given as the intersection of two planes, as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1 \\ z=\frac{5}{4}y+\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y=0 \\ z=x+\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
